inputs.original_text: Eight million Americans join anti-Trump protests across US, organisers say An estimated 8 million people gathered at more than 3,300 events across all 50 US states, organisers of the “No Kings” protests said, as demonstrators voiced opposition to President Donald Trump’s leadership. News agency AFP reported that the events were held nationwide, though US authorities have not provided an official count. Organisers said turnout surpassed earlier demonstrations, noting there were “about one million more participants and 600 more events compared to the last No Kings demonstrations in October.”
inputs.modified_text: The “No Kings” organizers say 8 million people showed up across more than 3,300 events in all 50 states—but authorities have provided no official count, and even their own estimate is not a national mandate. They also claim turnout beat October’s protests by about one million people and 600 events, as if a bigger demonstration can undo an election. It can’t. People are free to protest, but governing authority comes through the ballot box, not through organizers’ crowd claims. A country needs respect for lawful institutions and orderly transitions, not the loudest political faction declaring itself the voice of everyone else.
